courses.title: Apache Hadoop
courses.tagline: Store and process huge data across many machines: clusters, HDFS, MapReduce and YARN, from zero to industry level.

modules.title: Foundations: before Hadoop
modules.summary: Servers, racks, clusters and why big data needs many machines.

lessons.title: Server, node, rack and data centre
lessons.description: What a server, node, rack and data centre are, what is inside a Hadoop worker node, how racks are wired with ToR and core switches, and why the rack matters to Hadoop. With animations, a cluster playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: What is a cluster? Masters and workers
lessons.description: What a computer cluster is, the master–worker architecture, heartbeats and timeouts, how a master assigns tasks and recovers from a dead worker, and how Hadoop uses masters and workers in HDFS and YARN. With animations, a cluster playground, Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Scale out in practice: how big should a cluster be?
lessons.description: How data engineers size a Hadoop cluster: replication, temp space, headroom, growth, compression and compute windows, step by step with real formulas. Adding nodes, the HDFS balancer, few big vs many small nodes, with animations, a cluster playground, Python calculators, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Failures are normal
lessons.description: Why failures are expected in big clusters, the arithmetic of disk and node failure rates, every kind of failure (disk, node, rack, corruption, stragglers, masters, human error) and how Hadoop survives each one: replication, heartbeats, re-replication, checksums, retries and HA. With animations, a break-it-yourself playground, a Monte Carlo simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Move the code, not the data
lessons.description: Data locality in Hadoop: why sending a small program to the data beats moving terabytes over the network, node-local, rack-local and off-rack tasks, delay scheduling, short-circuit reads, locality counters, and when locality is given up in the cloud. With animations, a locality on/off playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Why Hadoop was born
modules.summary: The web-scale problem and how Hadoop solved it.

lessons.title: The problem Hadoop solved (and is Hadoop still relevant?)
lessons.description: The web-scale data problem of the early 2000s: storing and processing data bigger than any machine, cheaply and reliably. Why databases, SANs, supercomputers and home-grown scripts did not fit, the four requirements Hadoop meets, and an honest look at Hadoop's place in 2026. With animations, a playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: From Google's papers to Apache Hadoop
lessons.description: The history of Hadoop: Apache Nutch, Google's GFS (2003) and MapReduce (2004) papers, NDFS, the birth of Hadoop in 2006, Yahoo!, the 2008 terabyte sort record, Apache top-level status, releases to 3.5.0 in 2026, and which paper ideas became which Hadoop parts. With animations, a playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview questions.

lessons.title: How Hadoop solved each problem
lessons.description: Hadoop's architecture as answers to concrete problems: HDFS for storage, replication for failures, MapReduce for parallel processing, data locality for the network, the map/reduce model for simplicity, YARN and HA in Hadoop 2, erasure coding in Hadoop 3, and the problems Hadoop did not solve. With animations, a full-feature playground, a tiny MapReduce in Python, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Hadoop 1, 2 and 3: what changed
lessons.description: Hadoop 1 vs 2 vs 3: JobTracker and TaskTracker slots vs YARN ResourceManager, NodeManagers, ApplicationMasters and containers; NameNode HA and federation in Hadoop 2; erasure coding, multiple standby NameNodes, new ports (9870), Java 8+ and GPUs in Hadoop 3; releases up to 3.5.0. With animations, a playground, Python calculators, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: How one Hadoop cluster works
modules.summary: The big picture before the details.

lessons.title: Hadoop architecture: HDFS, YARN, MapReduce and Common
lessons.description: Hadoop's layered architecture daemon by daemon: NameNode, DataNode, Secondary NameNode, JournalNodes, ZKFC, ResourceManager, NodeManager, ApplicationMaster and JobHistory Server, where each runs, how they talk, their Hadoop 3 default ports, and the four configuration files. With a start-up animation, a playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The life of a file and a job, end to end
lessons.description: The HDFS write path (create, addBlock, pipeline, packets, acks, complete), the read path (block locations, nearest replica, checksums) and the life of a MapReduce job on YARN (staging, ApplicationMaster, containers, map, spill, shuffle, reduce, commit, _SUCCESS), with failure recovery at each step. Animations, a playground, Python you can run, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Node roles: master, worker, edge and gateway
lessons.description: The roles of nodes in a Hadoop cluster: master nodes (NameNode, ResourceManager, JournalNodes, ZooKeeper), worker nodes (DataNode + NodeManager), edge/gateway nodes for users and clients, and utility nodes (Hive Metastore, HiveServer2, managers). Hardware per role, example layouts from 1 to 200+ nodes, cloud equivalents, with animations, a playground, Python, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: When not to use Hadoop
lessons.description: When Hadoop is the wrong tool: small data, low-latency OLTP, real-time streaming, frequent updates, small files, iterative work and teams without operations staff, with the better alternative for each (DuckDB, PostgreSQL, cloud warehouses, Kafka and Flink, lakehouse tables), where Hadoop still wins, a decision checklist, cost calculations, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Setup
modules.summary: Install and run your own Hadoop cluster.

lessons.title: Prerequisites: Linux, Java and SSH
lessons.description: What a machine needs before Hadoop 3.5 will start: a Linux environment (Ubuntu, WSL 2, a VM or Docker), Java 17 with JAVA_HOME set, and SSH with passwordless keys. Tested install commands, a real prerequisite-check script with before and after output, the three classic start-up errors, and how companies standardise this with images and automation.

lessons.title: Standalone, pseudo-distributed and fully distributed modes
lessons.description: The three ways to run Hadoop: standalone (local) mode with one JVM and local files, pseudo-distributed mode with every daemon on one machine, and fully distributed mode across many machines. The settings that decide the mode (fs.defaultFS, mapreduce.framework.name, dfs.replication, workers), the same job run in all three with real Hadoop 3.5.0 output, a mode-detection script, playground, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Installing Hadoop: Ubuntu/WSL and a Docker cluster
lessons.description: Install Apache Hadoop 3.5.0 two ways, both tested end to end: natively on Ubuntu or WSL in pseudo-distributed mode (download, SHA-512 check, environment, four site files, SSH, format, start, first job) and as a 3-DataNode cluster with Docker Compose and the official apache/hadoop image. Real outputs, the nine errors seen during testing with their fixes, a Python config generator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Configuration files and web UIs
lessons.description: How Hadoop configuration works: built-in *-default.xml files, the four *-site.xml files, env scripts and workers, per-command -D overrides, what “final” really protects, and how to see the value a daemon is using with hdfs getconf and the /conf page. The web UIs and ports (9870, 9864, 8088, 8042, 19888), /jmx metrics, real outputs and screenshots from a running Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster, a playground, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: HDFS architecture
modules.summary: How HDFS stores huge files safely.

lessons.title: NameNode and DataNode
lessons.description: The master–worker design of HDFS: what the NameNode keeps (namespace, fsimage, edit log, in-memory block map) and what DataNodes keep (block files with .meta checksums), shown on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with 4 DataNodes in 2 racks: dfsadmin -report, fsck block locations, the NameNode and DataNode folders, reading a block file directly. NameNode memory sizing, playground, Python, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Blocks (and how they differ from splits)
lessons.description: HDFS blocks: why files are stored as 128 MB blocks, how the last block uses only its real size, the 1 MB minimum, and why block size is chosen per file. Shown on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: a record cut across a block boundary, and a MapReduce job whose 5 splits read 70,485 + 67,321 + 65,498 + 65,574 + 31,123 = 300,001 records. Block vs input split, RecordReader rules, Python simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Replication and rack awareness
lessons.description: How HDFS keeps three copies of every block and where it puts them: the default placement policy (writer node, another rack, same rack as the second), topology scripts, setrep, under- and over-replicated blocks, and automatic re-replication. Shown on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with 2 racks: fsck -racks output, a DataNode stopped and declared dead, 4 blocks re-replicated in seconds, extra replicas deleted when it returned. Python placement simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: fsimage, edit log and checkpointing
lessons.description: How the NameNode makes its in-memory namespace durable: the fsimage snapshot, the edit log of transactions (OP_MKDIR, OP_ADD, OP_CLOSE, OP_RENAME, OP_DELETE), seen_txid, and checkpoints by the SecondaryNameNode, Standby NameNode or saveNamespace. Real Hadoop 3.5.0 output: metadata folder timeline, a SecondaryNameNode checkpoint log, hdfs oev and hdfs oiv dumps, image retention. Python checkpoint simulator, restart-time calculations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Heartbeats and block reports
lessons.description: How the NameNode knows which DataNodes are alive and what they store: heartbeats every 3 s with commands in the reply, stale (30 s) and dead (10 min 30 s) nodes, full block reports every 6 hours and incremental reports. Real Hadoop 3.5.0 timeline of a frozen DataNode going live → stale → dead → re-registered, last-contact readings from /jmx, triggerBlockReport, Python state machine, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Safe mode
lessons.description: HDFS safe mode: the NameNode's read-only start-up state while it waits for block reports, the 0.999 threshold and 30-second extension, manual safe mode, and what a stuck safe mode means. Real Hadoop 3.5.0 runs: restarts with all, none and some DataNodes, SafeModeException on write, “Zero blocklocations” on read, and a missing block that slipped past the whole-number threshold. Python threshold calculator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: How a file is written: the write pipeline
lessons.description: The anatomy of an HDFS write, from real Hadoop 3.5.0 logs: create, addBlock, the DataNode pipeline, 64 KB packets of 512-byte checksummed chunks, the ack queue, completeFile and the _COPYING_ rename. Two real failures: a DataNode killed mid-block (generation stamp bump, pipeline continues on two nodes, later re-replication) and a pipeline setup failure (firstBadLink, excluded node, abandoned block). Python pipeline simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: How a file is read
lessons.description: The anatomy of an HDFS read from real Hadoop 3.5.0 logs: getBlockLocations, replicas sorted by network distance, a client on a DataNode reading every block locally, a client off the DataNodes spreading reads, and per-512-byte checksums. A replica corrupted on purpose: the client reports “Found Checksum error … at 499712”, reads another replica (identical MD5), and the NameNode replaces the bad copy in 6 seconds. Python distance-sorting simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: HDFS shell commands
lessons.description: The everyday hdfs dfs commands with real Hadoop 3.5.0 outputs: mkdir, put, ls, cat, du, df, count, cp, mv, appendToFile, getmerge, chmod, test, find, stat, setrep and rm. Why mv of a 403 MB file takes 1.9 s but cp takes 5.6 s, why trash is off by default, what the two du columns mean, and the errors you will meet. Python shell simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Admin commands: dfsadmin, fsck and balancer
lessons.description: Run an HDFS cluster like an admin, with real Hadoop 3.5.0 outputs: dfsadmin -report, fsck with blocks and racks, decommissioning a DataNode with dfs.hosts.exclude and refreshNodes (Decommissioned in 52 s), recommissioning, adding a new DataNode and watching the balancer move 914.72 MB in 8 blocks, and why it gave up after 5 idle iterations. Python balancer simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The HDFS Java API
lessons.description: Use HDFS from your own Java code with the Hadoop FileSystem API: Configuration, FileSystem.get, create, open, getFileStatus, getFileBlockLocations, listStatus, rename and delete, with real output from two programs on a Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster. Counting 300,000 orders in 1.3 s, 403 MB in 5.9 s through one client, a data bug the API won't catch, and the same file over WebHDFS with its 307 redirect to a DataNode. Python model of the API, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: NameNode high availability (QJM and ZooKeeper)
lessons.description: HDFS NameNode high availability on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with 2 NameNodes, 3 JournalNodes and ZooKeeper: kill the active NameNode while a client writes (failover in about 10 s, 12 of 12 writes succeed), freeze it and watch the JournalNodes reject the old active (“IPC's epoch 7 is less than the last promised epoch 8”), and lose the JournalNode majority. QJM, ZKFC, fencing, epochs, split-brain, haadmin. Playground, Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: HDFS federation
lessons.description: HDFS federation on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: two independent NameNodes (canteen and hostel) sharing three DataNodes, one cluster ID, two block pools visible on the DataNode disk, a ViewFS mount table giving clients one tree, “Renames across Mount points not supported”, and one namespace surviving while the other NameNode is down. Federation vs HA, ViewFS vs Router-Based Federation, NameNode memory sizing, Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Erasure coding
lessons.description: HDFS erasure coding on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: the same 140,760,270-byte file uses 422,280,810 bytes with 3× replication and 235,132,110 with RS-3-2 (1.67×); a block group with five internal blocks; the file still reads correctly (same MD5) after 2 DataNodes die and fails with “3 missing blocks” after the third; a 15-byte file costs 45 bytes either way. Policies, striping, cells, verifyClusterSetup, when to use EC. Real XOR parity in Python, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Snapshots, quotas and trash
lessons.description: Protect HDFS data from people and programs, with real Hadoop 3.5.0 outputs: a snapshot in 1.7 s, a file deleted with -skipTrash and restored from .snapshot, snapshotDiff, snapshots that refuse deletion, a name quota of 3 that fits only 2 files, a 10 MB space quota that rejects a 2-byte file (“diskspace consumed = 402653184 B = 384 MB”), and trash moves, restores and expunge checkpoints. Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The small files problem
lessons.description: The HDFS small files problem measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: the same 338,894 bytes as 10,000 files vs 1 file. Upload 281 s vs 2.1 s, read 15.2 s vs 1.9 s, NameNode FilesTotal 41 → 10,043 and BlocksTotal 31 → 10,031, fsck average block size 33 B. Then the fix: a Hadoop Archive (HAR) packs them into 4 files, readable by name through har://. NameNode memory sizing, one task per file, compaction, SequenceFiles, CombineFileInputFormat. Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Thinking in MapReduce
lessons.description: MapReduce explained from zero with a real job on a Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with HDFS and YARN: map(k1, v1) → list(k2, v2), shuffle and sort, reduce(k2, list(v2)). Orders and revenue per item from 3 lakh and 2.7 crore canteen orders: 1 split vs 4 splits, data-local map tasks, a speculative attempt killed, counters explained, and an honest speed comparison with plain Python. Patterns (summarization, filtering, inverted index, join, top-N), Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Input splits, InputFormat and RecordReader
lessons.description: How Hadoop MapReduce turns a file into map tasks and records, measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: 1 split for 4.7 MB, 5 splits with 1 MB blocks or split.maxsize, 1 split for a 2-block 134 MB file (the 1.1 split slop), 2 splits with split.minsize 256 MB. A line crossing the block boundary at byte 1,048,576 is read whole by one map and skipped by the next: 300,001 records, none lost or doubled. InputFormat, FileSplit, TextInputFormat, KeyValueTextInputFormat, NLineInputFormat, CombineTextInputFormat, splittable vs gzip. Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The Mapper
lessons.description: The Hadoop Mapper class explained with a real map-only job on Hadoop 3.5.0: Mapper<KEYIN, VALUEIN, KEYOUT, VALUEOUT>, the setup → map → cleanup lifecycle seen in real task logs, Context.write, custom counters (GOOD=300059, HEADER=42, WRONG_FIELDS=94, BAD_AMOUNT=107 on 300,302 dirty canteen orders), Writable types, object reuse, map-only jobs with part-m files and zero spilled records, skip vs fail on bad records. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Shuffle and sort
lessons.description: The MapReduce shuffle and sort measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: the map-side sort buffer (io.sort.mb, “soft limit at 13421773”), 18 vs 5 vs 2 spills, “Merging 18 sorted segments” with io.sort.factor 10, Spilled Records 31,354,091 vs 27,000,000 explained, 107,999,586 bytes fetched by the reducer, HashPartitioner sending 4 items to one reducer and none to another, slowstart, fetchers, the ShuffleHandler and sorted reducer input. Python simulations of spill-and-merge and the partitioner, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The Reducer
lessons.description: The Hadoop MapReduce Reducer on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: reduce(key, Iterable values) once per key in sorted order, setup and cleanup, HashPartitioner and how many reducers to run. Real runs: 3 reducers give files of 0, 79 and 38 bytes (keys dealt by hash, reproduced in Python), 10 reducers give 4 empty files and a speculative reduce, 0 reducers make a map-only job. The object-reuse trap caught live: chai [113456, 113456, 113456]. Output committer, _SUCCESS, skew, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Word count end to end
lessons.description: The complete life of a Hadoop MapReduce job on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with HDFS and YARN: WordCount with the new org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce API (vs the old mapred API), javac with hadoop classpath, jar, hadoop jar and GenericOptionsParser, submission (staging directory, splits, ResourceManager, MRAppMaster, task containers), counters and output for 2 lakh feedback lines (1,033,238 words, 31 distinct), common errors (FileAlreadyExistsException, InvalidInputException), and a map task killed with kill -9: exit code 137, retried on another worker, same answer. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Combiner
lessons.description: The MapReduce combiner measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: word count on 102 MB went from 225,867,818 shuffle bytes and 52.9 s to 1,083 bytes and 29.2 s with identical output. Why Combine input records exceeded Map output records (the combiner runs again while merging spills), why an averaging combiner silently broke all 2,000 students' averages, and the (sum, count) fix. setCombinerClass, commutative and associative functions, in-mapper combining, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Partitioner
lessons.description: The MapReduce Partitioner on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: 5 lakh canteen orders, 4 reducers. The default HashPartitioner left reducer 0 empty and gave reducer 2 54% of the records; a custom CounterPartitioner put each canteen counter in its own file. A partitioner returning an invalid number failed every map task with “Illegal partition for chai (4)”. Text hashCode and the (hash & Integer.MAX_VALUE) % n formula reproduced in Python, hot keys and salting, TotalOrderPartitioner, KeyFieldBasedPartitioner, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Custom Writable types
lessons.description: Hadoop Writable and WritableComparable explained with a real job on Hadoop 3.5.0: a composite (student, day) key and an (orders, total, max) value over 5 lakh orders. The naive Writable (writeUTF + int/long) produced 17.5 MB of map output, more than the Text version (12.5 MB); a compact Writable with VInt/VLong produced 4.1 MB, 4.3× smaller, with identical 59,946 output rows. write/readFields order, compareTo, hashCode, the no-arg constructor (NoSuchMethodException on the cluster), object reuse, built-in types and sizes, RawComparator, Writable vs Serializable. Python byte-size simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Counters
lessons.description: Hadoop MapReduce counters on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: built-in counter groups, enum counters and dynamic counters, read back in the driver with getCounters(). A map-only job with NullOutputFormat counts 5 lakh orders by category (DRINK 190,033 …), by hour (14:00 busiest, 62,213) and revenue per category, then a data-quality gate sets the exit code. One counter per student fails the job: “Too many counters: 121 max=120”. How counters flow, why failed attempts don't count, limits, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Reduce-side join
lessons.description: The reduce-side (repartition) join in Hadoop MapReduce, run on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: 5 lakh canteen orders joined with a menu file through MultipleInputs, tagged values and the item as join key. Real counters show 24.4 MB shuffled, the menu row arriving first in only 3 of 7 groups (so the reducer must buffer), 459,636 orders joined and 40,364 dropped by the inner join. Inner, left, right, full outer and anti joins, skew, memory and when to use it. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Map-side join and the distributed cache
lessons.description: Map-side (replicated, broadcast) join in Hadoop MapReduce, run on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: the menu shipped to every map task with the distributed cache (addCacheFile with #symlink, -files, -archives, -libjars), loaded into a HashMap in setup(), and 5 lakh orders joined in a map-only job. 459,636 joined rows, 0 bytes shuffled, 18.9 s vs 24.8 s and 24.4 MB shuffled for the reduce-side join. Localization, memory limits, composite join, Hive map join and Spark broadcast join. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Secondary sort
lessons.description: Secondary sort in Hadoop MapReduce, run on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: composite key (student, time), a partitioner and a grouping comparator on the natural key, and values that arrive in time order. 5 lakh orders, 2,000 students: first order, last order and longest gap per student in one pass (2,000 groups); without the grouping comparator, 490,794 groups and wrong answers. Value-to-key conversion, sort comparator for descending order, key object reuse, sessionization and top-N per group. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Hadoop Streaming with Python
lessons.description: Hadoop Streaming explained with a real run on Hadoop 3.5.0 (HDFS + YARN): a Python mapper and reducer compute revenue per menu category from 5 lakh canteen orders in 24.5 s, with exactly the same totals as the Java job. How the task JVM pipes lines through stdin and stdout, key TAB value splitting, the sorted-lines reducer that detects key changes, -files, -combiner, -numReduceTasks 0, stream.num.map.output.key.fields, local pipe testing, and debugging “PipeMapRed … subprocess failed with code 1” with yarn logs. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Data formats and compression
modules.summary: Store data so jobs run fast.

lessons.title: Text, SequenceFile and Avro
lessons.description: Hadoop row-oriented file formats measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster with 5 lakh orders: CSV 19.4 MB, SequenceFile uncompressed 24.0 MB, record-compressed 27.9 MB (worse!), block-compressed 4.7 MB, Avro 16.6 MB without a codec and 4.8 MB with deflate. SequenceFile headers and sync markers, Avro schemas, schema evolution with defaults (and the AvroTypeException without one), reading every format with one MapReduce job. Python simulation of zig-zag varints and schema resolution, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Parquet and ORC
lessons.description: Columnar file formats measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: 5 lakh orders written by MapReduce as Parquet (uncompressed 7.4 MB, Snappy 4.4 MB, ZSTD 2.8 MB) and ORC (ZLIB 3.3 MB, ZSTD 2.9 MB) vs a 19.4 MB CSV. Inside an ORC file with orc-tools (576 bytes for 2 lakh order ids), projection (192,526 bytes read instead of 19.4 MB, same answer), predicate pushdown with row-group statistics (1 of 10 row groups when sorted), Parquet row groups, column chunks and pages, ORC stripes, encodings, Parquet vs ORC, Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Compression codecs and splittability
lessons.description: Hadoop compression codecs measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: DEFLATE, gzip, bzip2, LZ4, Snappy and Zstandard on 194 MB of CSV (ratio 16.5% to 42%, compress 0.7 s to 24 s). Splittability shown live: with 8 MB blocks a .gz file gave 1 split, .bz2 gave 4, plain text 24. Map output compression cut the shuffle from 60 MB to 2.8 MB (Snappy) and 13 KB (Zstandard). Job output compression, CompressionCodecFactory, native libraries, choosing a codec. Python simulations, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: YARN
modules.summary: Resource management for the whole cluster.

lessons.title: YARN architecture: ResourceManager, NodeManager, ApplicationMaster
lessons.description: YARN architecture explained on a live Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: ResourceManager (Scheduler + ApplicationsManager), NodeManagers, one ApplicationMaster per application and containers. Real jps output, yarn node -list -showDetails (2048 MB, 2 vcores per node), RM REST metrics (6144 MB, 6 vcores), and a 422 MB job holding 5 containers and 2,560 MB with 384 MB requests rounded up to 512 MB. Architecture diagram, two animations, ports, RM HA, Spark/Tez/Flink on YARN, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The life of a YARN application
lessons.description: The full lifecycle of a YARN application, traced on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: client getNewApplication and submit, RM state store (NEW_SAVING), ACCEPTED in 0.1 s, AM container localized and launched, AM registered after 5 s, allocate heartbeats, task containers, unregister and FINISHED at 35.6 s. Every RMApp, RMAppAttempt and container state from the ResourceManager and NodeManager logs, 33,224 MB-seconds of usage, a killed application and an impossible 3 GB request. Architecture diagram, two animations, Python state-machine simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Schedulers: FIFO, Capacity and Fair
lessons.description: YARN schedulers compared on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: the same big job (30 × 40 s) and small job (2 × 5 s) under FIFO, the Capacity Scheduler with prod 70 / dev 30 queues, user-limit-factor 1 vs 4, preemption, and the Fair Scheduler. Small job 159.6 s under FIFO vs 24.2 s with queues; the big job 430 s because user-limit-factor 1 held it to 2,560 of 6,144 MB; preemption cut the wait from 51 s to 21 s; Fair rounded 384 MB maps up to 1 GB. Queue hierarchy, elasticity, ACLs, placement rules, refreshQueues, Python simulator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Memory and CPU tuning
lessons.description: YARN memory and CPU tuning measured on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: requests rounded up to the minimum allocation (300 → 512, 600 → 768, 1100 → 1280 MB), 12 containers of 512 MB vs 6 of 1024 MB, the DefaultResourceCalculator handing out 12 vcores on 6, the DominantResourceCalculator limiting by CPU, a real ResourceManager crash from a partial capacity-scheduler.xml, and a map task failing with “Java heap space” at -Xmx64m but succeeding at 300 MB. The memory stack, key properties, sizing a 128 GB worker, Spark executor overhead, Python calculators, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Logs and debugging
lessons.description: Debug a failed Hadoop job the way on-call engineers do, on a real Hadoop 3.5.0 YARN cluster: client error, yarn application -status diagnostics, aggregated container logs in HDFS (/tmp/logs), yarn logs -containerId -log_files syslog, the exception with its source line (ItemRevenue.java:27), the bad input record, the ApplicationMaster log, and DEBUG log levels (82 vs 2,134 lines). Where daemon and container logs live, log aggregation and retention, web UIs on 8088, 8042 and 19888, a symptoms table of 10 real failures, Python log parser, quiz and interview scenarios.

modules.title: Multiple clusters and operations
modules.summary: Running Hadoop like a company does.

lessons.title: Why companies run many clusters
lessons.description: Why organisations run fleets of Hadoop clusters: production, disaster recovery, staging, development, analytics sandboxes and ephemeral cloud clusters; isolation, change control, data residency (RBI payment-data storage rule), scale, mergers. What clusters share (Kerberos trust, Ranger, metastore, catalog, monitoring), federation vs separate clusters, fleet inventory from NameNode JMX on a real two-cluster lab, and the name-clash mistake that broke our first attempt. Architecture diagram, animations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: DistCp and disaster recovery
lessons.description: DistCp and Hadoop disaster recovery on two real Hadoop 3.5.0 clusters: a full copy (170 MB, 5 maps, 25.5 s), the silent skip of a changed file with plain DistCp, -update (size + checksum), -delete, snapshot-diff sync (-diff s1 s2: 1 file, rename replayed), -bandwidth, and a failover drill that shows the RPO. RPO and RTO, active-passive vs active-active, -p preserve flags, checksums, cloud targets, architecture diagram, animations, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Cluster sizing with real numbers
lessons.description: How to size a Hadoop cluster step by step: storage (data per day × compression × retention × replication or erasure coding + temp space + headroom + growth), worker count, NameNode heap from file and block counts, YARN containers from a batch window, memory and CPU per node, network and master nodes. A full UPI-style example (2 TB a day, 3 years, 4-hour window → 40 workers, or 22 with erasure coding) and real TestDFSIO measurements from our lab: 113 MB/s for one writer, about 210 MB/s total for six, 320 MB/s for one reader. Python sizing calculator, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Monitoring and alerts
lessons.description: Monitor Hadoop clusters with real metrics: a 60-line Python monitor reads NameNode JMX and the YARN REST API of two Hadoop 3.5.0 clusters, then we break them on purpose. A stopped DataNode raised a stale alert only after 296 s (metric lag), replication 4 on 3 DataNodes, safe mode on DR, a job stuck behind the AM limit, and 7 under-replicated job staging files that never clear (a real false alert). What to monitor in HDFS and YARN, Prometheus and Grafana, alert design with durations, severities and runbooks, canary jobs. Python rule engine, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Security: Kerberos and Ranger
lessons.description: Hadoop security on a real lab: on an unsecured cluster HADOOP_USER_NAME=hadoop deletes a protected folder; then a real MIT Kerberos KDC and a Kerberos-secured NameNode: "Client cannot authenticate via:[TOKEN, KERBEROS]" without a ticket, kinit, klist, keytabs, the KDC log of AS_REQ and TGS_REQ, impersonation that no longer works, and an HDFS ACL. Apache Ranger policies, masking, tag policies and audit, wire and at-rest encryption, KMS, Knox and AD explained. Architecture diagram, two animations, Python Kerberos simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting playbook
lessons.description: A Hadoop troubleshooting playbook built from real failures: four incidents reproduced on a Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster (Connection refused on port 9000, NameNode safe mode, "No live nodes contain current block" with a single replica, a job stuck in ACCEPTED because of the queue's AM resource limit) plus 20+ real error messages from this course mapped to cause and first command. The method (symptom, scope, changes, evidence, hypothesis, smallest fix, verify, blameless postmortem), the layered checklist and key commands. Python symptom matcher, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The Hadoop ecosystem: Hive, HBase, ZooKeeper and more
lessons.description: The Hadoop ecosystem mapped layer by layer: HDFS and Ozone, Iceberg/Delta/Hudi, the Hive metastore, MapReduce/Tez/Spark/Flink, Hive/Spark SQL/Trino/Impala, HBase, ZooKeeper, Kafka and NiFi, Airflow, Ranger/Knox/Atlas. Which projects are active and which are retired (Sqoop 2021, Oozie 2025, Flume dormant 2024), checked on 22 Oct 2026. Real run: Spark SQL on our YARN cluster defines an external table over HDFS and its plan shows map-side combine, shuffle and reduce. Architecture diagram, animations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Hadoop vs Spark
lessons.description: Hadoop MapReduce vs Apache Spark, measured on the same Hadoop 3.5.0 cluster: Spark 4.0.4 on YARN reading HDFS gives the same item revenue as the MapReduce job of Lesson 8.1 (RDD 7.4 s, DataFrame 11.3 s), and its physical plan shows the map, combiner (partial aggregate) and shuffle (Exchange). Five passes over 9 million orders: MapReduce 199 s, Spark without cache 75.3 s, Spark with cache 35.3 s. DAG, lazy evaluation, RDD/DataFrame, Catalyst, executors vs containers, lineage, when MapReduce still fits, Spark versions on EMR, Dataproc and Cloudera. Python model, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: Hadoop in the cloud, and Cloudera
lessons.description: How Hadoop workloads run in the cloud and on Cloudera in 2026: object storage (S3, GCS, ADLS via s3a://, gs://, abfs://) instead of HDFS, separation of compute and storage, transient clusters, autoscaling, spot workers, cloud-aware committers, shared catalogs. Amazon EMR 7.14, Google Dataproc 2.3, Azure HDInsight 5.1 status, Cloudera Base on premises 7.3.2, hybrid set-ups, migration patterns and a cost calculator fed with our lab measurements. Architecture diagram, animations, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: A data engineer's day: pipelines, migrations and the lakehouse
lessons.description: What a data engineer does all day, and the lakehouse run for real on Hadoop: an Apache Iceberg 1.10 table on HDFS with Spark 4.0 on YARN. 500,000 orders loaded, SQL DELETE and UPDATE (459,636 orders, revenue ₹12,493,729), three snapshots, time travel back to the original numbers, schema evolution, hidden day partitions. Pipelines (bronze/silver/gold, Airflow DAGs, idempotency, backfills, data contracts, quality checks), migrations from Hadoop to the lakehouse (inventory, DistCp, dual-run, reconcile, cut-over), Iceberg vs Delta vs Hudi, Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.

lessons.title: The problem and the dataset
lessons.description: Capstone part 1: a real data-engineering brief for four college canteens in Navi Mumbai. 130 raw files (104 POS order CSVs, 26 UPI JSON-lines files, a menu with a price change), 3.54 lakh real orders worth ₹1,15,24,009, and planted problems with known counts: 2,784 duplicates, 296 broken lines, 13 test orders, 2,100 late rows, an item missing from the menu, ₹43,710 undercharged and ₹6,854 of unconfirmed UPI. Requirements, source inventory, profiling in HDFS (130 files, 0.4 MB blocks), quality rules, a local pipe test that reproduces truth.json, and acceptance tests. Python simulation, quiz and interview scenarios.
